2027-01-20.title: Wednesday of the Second Week in Ordinary Time · Sts Fabian and Sebastian
readings: A priest for ever, like Melchizedek
You are a priest for ever, in the line of Melchizedek
Is it lawful to do good on the sabbath?
2027-01-20.alt: Weekday of Ordinary Time, Week 2 (Year I). Liturgical colour: green. Week of Prayer for Christian Unity (18–25 January). Optional memorials: St Fabian, pope and martyr; St Sebastian, martyr. In India St Sebastian is widely celebrated.
2027-01-20.verse: Then he said to them, “Is it lawful to do good or to do harm on the sabbath, to save life or to kill?” But they were silent.
theo: Hebrews reflects on the mysterious king Melchizedek, who “brought out bread and wine” and blessed Abraham. He appears in Scripture “without father, without mother, without genealogy”, and so “resembling the Son of God, he remains a priest forever.” Christ is a priest not by family descent like the Levites, but “through the power of an indestructible life”. The Church has always seen in Melchizedek's bread and wine a sign of the Eucharist.

In the synagogue a man with a withered hand stands before Jesus while his critics watch. Jesus asks: “Is it lawful to do good or to do harm on the sabbath, to save life or to kill?” They are silent. Mark says Jesus looked at them “with anger; he was grieved at their hardness of heart”, and healed the man. Hardness of heart grieves God more than any broken rule. Today many in Kerala honour St Sebastian, the soldier who served Christ before the emperor and gave his life rather than deny him, and St Fabian, pope and martyr. Both had hearts that were soft toward God and firm in the truth.
outline: Ask: what makes a heart hard?
Point 2 · Grieved at hardness of heart
“Is it lawful to do good… to save life?”
live: Ask God to show you one area where your heart has grown hard.
Defend someone who is treated unjustly at work or school.
2027-01-20.prayer: Lord Jesus, eternal priest like Melchizedek, you were grieved at hardness of heart. Soften my heart, give me courage like St Sebastian, and let me always choose to do good and to save life. Amen.
altar: Melchizedek offered bread and wine; Christ, priest for ever, offers his Body and Blood under these signs (Roman Canon).

quick: Christ is a priest for ever, like Melchizedek.
Jesus grieves over hardness of heart and heals.
Sebastian and Fabian were brave soldiers of Christ.

2027-01-20.question: Where has my heart grown hard?

family.explain: A man had a hand that did not work. Some people did not want Jesus to heal on the sabbath. Jesus was sad that their hearts were hard, and he healed the man.
family.intention: We pray for soldiers, police and all who protect others.
family.ask: Ask: “How can we be brave like St Sebastian?”

illus: Across Kerala, St Sebastian's feasts fill streets with processions and arrows decorated with flowers. An old parish priest used to tell children: Sebastian was shot with arrows and survived, then went back to tell the emperor the truth. Real courage is going back to do what is right.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, priest for ever, soften our hearts and make us brave witnesses like St Sebastian. Amen.
share: A priest forever, according to the order of Melchizedek (Psalm 110:4). What does Christ's priesthood mean for me?
He was grieved at their hardness of heart (Mark 3:5). Where is my heart hard?
Share in suffering like a good soldier of Christ Jesus (2 Timothy 2:3). Where do I need courage?
pm.resp: Lord, give us hearts of flesh.
interc: For soldiers and police, through St Sebastian.
For the Pope, through St Fabian.
pm.close: Father, your Son is priest for ever and healer of hearts. Make us soft toward you and brave in witness. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

homily: Dear friends, Hebrews tells us of Melchizedek, king of Salem, who brought out bread and wine and blessed Abraham. He appears without father, without mother, without genealogy, and so, resembling the Son of God, he remains a priest forever (Hebrews 7:3).
Christ is a priest not by family descent, but through the power of an indestructible life. And the bread and wine of Melchizedek point to the Eucharist.

In the Gospel Jesus asks: is it lawful to do good or to do harm on the sabbath, to save life or to kill? But they were silent (Mark 3:4). He looked at them with anger, grieved at their hardness of heart, and healed the withered hand.

Today we honour St Fabian, a pope who died a martyr, and St Sebastian, the Roman soldier loved across Kerala, who served Christ before the emperor and gave his life rather than deny him. Let us ask for hearts soft toward God and firm in courage. Amen.
kids: Children, St Sebastian was a brave soldier for Jesus. Be brave too: stand up for a friend who is being teased.

intro: Theme: “Is it lawful to do good or to do harm on the sabbath, to save life or to kill?”
The eternal priest, the hardened heart, the brave martyrs.

q: And King Melchizedek of Salem brought out bread and wine; he was priest of God Most High.

It is even more obvious when another priest arises, resembling Melchizedek, one who has become a priest, not through a legal requirement concerning physical descent, but through the power of an indestructible life.
points.apply: Thank Christ the priest at Mass this week.

q: I will give them one heart, and put a new spirit within them; I will remove the heart of stone from their flesh and give them a heart of flesh,
He looked around at them with anger; he was grieved at their hardness of heart and said to the man, “Stretch out your hand.” He stretched it out, and his hand was restored.
points.apply: Ask God to soften one hard place in your heart.

q: I hereby command you: Be strong and courageous; do not be frightened or dismayed, for the LORD your God is with you wherever you go.”
Share in suffering like a good soldier of Christ Jesus.

concl: Christ the priest heals hardened hearts.
Sebastian and Fabian show the courage of soft hearts.
2027-01-20.resolve: Choose always to do good and save life this week.
